steps: Boil a kettle and bring a large pan of unsalted water to the boil for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin, short strips about 1cm wide, suitable for small mouths.
Cut the red pepper into short thin strips and grate or julienne the carrot finely so it softens quickly.
Cook the noodles in the unsalted water for 4 minutes or to packet timing, then drain and snip into short lengths.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes, until white with no pink inside.
Add the carrot and pepper and cook for 3–4 minutes until soft, then toss in the noodles with the soy sauce diluted with a splash of water.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of undiluted soy sauce makes the dish far too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and taste.
Leaving chicken or carrot in large or thick pieces creates a choking risk and uneven cooking, so cut everything small and soft.
Overcrowding the wok steams the chicken instead of searing it, leaving it pale and rubbery.
output.tip: Cool a portion for a few minutes and check the chicken is cooked through and not too hot before serving to your toddler.

steps: Boil a kettle of water and put the noodles in a large saucepan on the hob.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, so it is easy for a toddler to chew.
Cut the red peppers and carrots into thin matchsticks or small pieces, no longer than 3cm.
Cook the noodles for 4–5 minutes until soft, then drain and snip them into short lengths.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots for 3 minutes, then the red pepper for 2 minutes until soft. Stir in the noodles with the soy sauce diluted in a splash of water, and toss for 1 minute.
pitfalls: Adding the soy sauce undiluted makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and add it a little at a time.
Leaving noodles and vegetables in long strands or hard chunks is a choking risk, so cut them short and cook the carrots until soft.
Overcrowding the wok steams the chicken and leaves it pale and rubbery, so cook it in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Let the stir-fry cool for a few minutes and check that the chicken is cooked through before serving it to a toddler.

steps: Boil a kettle and start the noodles in a large saucepan, following the pack time, then drain and toss with a drizzle of oil.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, so they are easy for a toddler to chew.
Cut the red peppers into thin short strips and grate or thinly slice the carrots into matchsticks, so they cook quickly and soften.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots, then the peppers, and stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until soft enough to squash between your fingers.
Stir in the noodles with the soy sauce and a splash of water from the kettle, toss for 1 minute, then cool before serving.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so use it sparingly and loosen with water.
Cutting vegetables into thick chunks leaves them firm and hard to chew, so keep them thin and cook until soft.
Overcooking the chicken makes it dry and tough, so slice it thinly and take it off as soon as no pink remains.
output.tip: Cut the noodles into shorter lengths with kitchen scissors before serving, so they are easier for a toddler to eat.

steps: Fill the large saucepan with salted water and bring to the boil over a high heat.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat, then brown the beef mince for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up.
Stir in the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and pepper, then simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 1 minute less than the packet time, reserve a mug of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the frying pan makes the beef mince steam and turn grey, so brown it in two batches if needed.
Burnt garlic turns bitter and spoils the sauce, so add it only for the last minute before the tomatoes.
Rinsing the spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Finish the spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water for 1 minute so it coats every strand.

steps: Dice the onion finely and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat, then fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the beef mince, breaking it up and browning it for 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the sauce simmers, boil the water in the saucepan, salt it generously and cook the spaghetti for 9–11 minutes until al dente.
Drain the spaghetti, reserving a mugful of cooking water, then toss it with the sauce, loosening with the water if needed.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so let it sit undisturbed before breaking it up.
Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only after the onion has softened and cook it for 1 minute.
Rinsing the spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Simmer the sauce for the full 20 minutes, as the longer it reduces the richer and sweeter it tastes.

steps: Fill the large saucepan with water and bring it to the boil on the hob.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the beef mince over high heat, breaking it up and browning for 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Salt the boiling water and cook the spaghetti 10–12 minutes until al dente, then drain, saving a mugful of water.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey instead of browning, so the sauce lacks depth of flavour.
Under-seasoning the pasta water leaves the spaghetti bland, so salt it generously once it boils.
Rushing the simmer leaves a thin, acidic sauce that slides off the pasta, so give it the full 20 minutes.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of the reserved pasta water so it clings to every strand.

steps: Boil a large pan of water, then salt it generously.
Add the spaghetti and cook for 1 minute less than the packet time, until just short of tender.
While the water heats, drain the tuna and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over low–medium heat for 1 minute.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the spaghetti and tuna in the frying pan for 1–2 minutes, loosening with splashes of pasta water until glossy.
pitfalls: Overheating the tuna dries it out and makes it crumbly, so only warm it through.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the dish dry and oily, so keep a mugful back.
Under-salting the pasta water leaves the spaghetti bland, as the tuna cannot make up for it.
output.tip: Finish the spaghetti in the pan with a little starchy pasta water so the oil clings to every strand.

steps: Bring a large pan of water to the boil on the hob and salt it well.
Add the spaghetti and cook for 1 minute less than the packet time, stirring in the first 30 seconds.
While the pasta cooks, drain the tuna and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over low-medium heat, then add the tuna for 2 minutes, just until warmed through.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the spaghetti in the frying pan with the tuna and a splash of pasta water for 1 minute, until glossy.
pitfalls: Cooking the spaghetti to the full packet time leaves it soft once it finishes in the pan, so stop 1 minute early.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the dish dry and oily, so keep a mugful to loosen it.
Frying the tuna over high heat for too long makes it dry and crumbly, so only warm it gently.
output.tip: Taste before adding any extra salt at the end, as the tuna and the seasoned pasta water already bring plenty.

steps: Boil plenty of water in the large saucepan over a high heat, then add the salt.
Cook the spaghetti for 1 minute less than the packet time, until just short of tender.
While the water heats, drain the tuna and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a low–medium heat for 1 minute.
Reserve a mugful of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and toss it in the pan with the tuna.
Add a splash of pasta water and toss over a low heat for 1 minute, until glossy.
pitfalls: Overheating the tuna dries it out and makes it chalky, so only warm it through for 1–2 minutes.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the dish dry and oily, so keep some to loosen the sauce.
Overcooking the spaghetti turns it soft and mushy once it finishes in the pan, so pull it early.
output.tip: Toss the pasta and tuna off the heat at the end so the starchy water and oil emulsify into a light coating.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C, then rub the beef with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper, and leave it at room temperature.
Parboil the peeled, chunked potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain, shake to rough the edges, and heat oil in a baking tray in the oven.
Roast the beef for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C and cook for about 1 hour 10 minutes for medium (60°C core).
Roast the potatoes and parsnips in the hot oil for 50–60 minutes, turning once, while you whisk the batter and rest it for 30 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes, then raise the oven to 220°C and heat oil in the pudding tin for 10 minutes before pouring in the batter.
Bake the puddings for 20–25 minutes, boil the carrots and broccoli, and make gravy in the roasting tin with wine, stock and butter.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so wait at least 20 minutes.
Pouring batter into lukewarm oil gives flat, greasy puddings, so the oil must be smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Whisk a spoonful of plain flour into the roasting tin juices before adding the wine, then simmer for 5 minutes for smooth, glossy gravy.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, then rub with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper. Heat the oven to 220°C.
Make the Yorkshire batter by whisking flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt. Rest it at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
Sear the beef in the roasting tin for 20 minutes at 220°C, then lower to 180°C. Roast for about 1 hour 10 minutes for medium, until 55–60°C in the centre.
Parboil the peeled potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake to roughen the edges. Roast in hot oil on the heavy tray at 200°C for 60 minutes, turning once, with the parsnips from 30 minutes in.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the pudding tin for 10 minutes, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.

While the puddings bake, simmer the carrots for 10 minutes and steam the broccoli for 4 minutes. Deglaze the roasting tin on the hob with wine, add stock and butter, then simmer the gravy for 10 minutes and strain it.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so wait until they are golden and set.
Pouring batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so the oil must be smoking hot first.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the resting time to free up the oven for the Yorkshire puddings, and keep the potatoes warm on the top shelf.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, then rub with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and seasoning. Heat the oven to 220°C.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and cook 50–60 minutes for medium. Rest it under foil for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and cut the potatoes and parsnips, parboil the potatoes for 8–10 minutes, then drain and shake to roughen the edges.
Heat oil in a baking tray until smoking, then add the potatoes and parsnips. Roast for 50–60 minutes at 200°C, turning once, and add the carrots for the final 40 minutes.

Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and seasoning into a batter and rest it. When the beef comes out, raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tin until smoking, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.
While the puddings bake, simmer the roasting tin juices with wine and stock for 10 minutes to make the gravy. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes, then carve the beef and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise lets the heat escape, so they collapse and turn dense.
Pouring batter into oil that is not smoking hot gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the tin for at least 5 minutes.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the slices dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Add a knob of butter and a splash of the beef resting juices to the gravy at the end for a glossy, richer finish.

steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt and half the tikka paste in a bowl, then marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Cook the rest of the paste in a wide pan over medium heat for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chicken with its marinade and brown for 5 minutes, then pour in the tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
While the curry simmers, cook the rice following the packet instructions, then serve the curry over the rice.
pitfalls: Boiling the sauce hard after adding the marinade can split the yoghurt, so keep it at a gentle simmer.
Cooking the paste over high heat scorches it and makes the sauce bitter.
Crowding the pan steams the chicken instead of browning it, so use a wide pan or brown in two batches.
output.tip: Rest the finished curry off the heat for 5 minutes so the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken stays juicy.

steps: Cut the chicken into 3cm pieces, then mix with the yoghurt and half the tikka paste. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the rest of the paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Add the chicken with its marinade and brown it, then pour in the tomatoes. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with 600ml water, covered, on low heat for 12 minutes. Serve the curry over the rice.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan steams the chicken instead of browning it, so brown it in two batches if it does not fit in one layer.
Boiling the sauce hard makes the chicken tough and the sauce catch on the base, so keep it at a gentle simmer.
Lifting the lid while the rice cooks lets the steam out and leaves it unevenly cooked.
output.tip: Rest the finished curry off the heat for 5 minutes so the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken stays juicy.

steps: Cut the chicken into 3cm pieces and marinate in the yoghurt and half the tikka paste for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the frying pan over medium heat, add the rest of the paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Add the chicken with its marinade and brown it, then pour in the tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Boil the rice for 10–12 minutes while the curry simmers, then drain and serve with the curry.
pitfalls: Cooking the paste over high heat scorches the spices and makes the sauce bitter.
Crowding the pan steams the chicken instead of browning it, so use a wide pan.
Boiling the curry hard instead of simmering toughens the chicken and splits the yoghurt, leaving a grainy sauce.
output.tip: Rest the curry off the heat for 5 minutes before serving so the sauce thickens and the chicken stays juicy.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Pat the chicken dry, then rub with half the olive oil and half the salt.
Sear the chicken in the oven-safe pan over high heat (about 220°C) for 3 minutes.
Roast the chicken in the oven at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Rest the chicken on a board while the beans boil in salted water for 4–5 minutes, then drain.
Toss the beans with the remaining oil and a squeeze of lemon, then slice the chicken and serve with lemon wedges.
pitfalls: Cramming wet chicken into the pan steams it instead of searing, so it stays pale; dry it thoroughly first.
Slicing the chicken straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so rest it first.
Overboiling the beans turns them dull and limp; drain them as soon as they are just tender.
output.tip: Plunge the drained beans into cold water for 30 seconds to keep their bright green colour, then toss them in the oil.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Season the chicken with salt and a little of the olive oil.
Sear the chicken in the oven-safe frying pan at 220°C for 3 minutes.
Roast the chicken at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Rest the chicken while the trimmed green beans boil in salted water until just tender.
Drain the beans, toss with the remaining oil and a squeeze of lemon, then serve with the sliced chicken and lemon wedges.
pitfalls: Slicing the chicken straight from the oven lets the juices run out, leaving it dry.
Overcooking the beans turns them dull and limp, so test one after 4 minutes.
Crowding the pan or starting with wet chicken stops it browning, so pat it dry first.
output.tip: Check that the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C with a probe thermometer before resting.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and bring a large pan of salted water to the boil for the beans.
Pat the chicken dry, then rub with half the olive oil and the salt.
Sear the chicken in a very hot oven-safe frying pan at 220°C for 3 minutes.
Transfer the pan to the oven and roast the chicken at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Rest the chicken on a board while you boil the trimmed beans until tender-crisp, then drain.
Toss the beans with the remaining oil and a squeeze of lemon, slice the chicken, and serve with lemon wedges.
pitfalls: Overcooking the beans turns them dull and limp, so drain them as soon as they are tender-crisp.
Cutting the chicken straight from the pan lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so let it rest first.
Putting wet chicken in the pan steams it instead of browning it, so dry it thoroughly.
output.tip: Check the thickest part of the chicken with a thermometer for 75°C, or cut in to confirm the juices run clear.

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into even 4cm chunks, then cover with cold salted water in the saucepan.
Bring the potatoes to the boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
While the potatoes heat, grate or finely chop the onion and mix with the beef mince, egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Roll the mixture into 16–20 even balls, about 4cm wide, with damp hands.
Fry the meatballs in a little oil over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season well and serve with the meatballs and ketchup on the side.
pitfalls: Overmixing the meatball mixture makes the meatballs dense and tough, so mix only until combined.
Cold milk added to the potatoes cools the mash and makes it gluey, so warm it first.
Crowding the frying pan steams the meatballs instead of browning them, so cook in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Dry the drained potatoes in the hot pan for a minute before mashing for a fluffier, less watery mash.

steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into even 4cm chunks, cover with cold salted water, bring to the boil, then simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender.
While the potatoes cook, grate or finely chop the onion and soften it in a little butter over medium heat for 5 minutes. Leave to cool briefly.
Mix the beef mince, egg, breadcrumbs, cooled onion, salt and pepper in a bowl until just combined.
Roll the mixture into 16–20 even balls, about 3cm wide.
Fry the meatballs in a little oil over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning often, until browned all over and cooked through.
Drain the potatoes well and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth, then season. Serve with the meatballs and ketchup on the side.
pitfalls: Overworking the meat mixture makes the meatballs dense and tough, so mix only until combined.
Adding cold milk to the potatoes cools them and makes the mash gluey, so warm the milk first.
Crowding the frying pan steams the meatballs instead of browning them, so fry in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Let the drained potatoes steam dry in the warm pan for 2 minutes before mashing for a fluffier, less watery mash.

steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into 4cm chunks, then cover with cold salted water in the saucepan.
Bring the potatoes to the boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
While the potatoes cook, finely chop the onion and mix with the beef mince, egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture into 16–20 even balls, about 4cm wide.
Fry the meatballs in a little oil over medium heat for 12–15 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and warmed milk until smooth. Season to taste and serve with the meatballs and ketchup on the side.
pitfalls: Overmixing the meatball mixture makes the meatballs dense and tough, so combine until just mixed.
Cooking the meatballs over too high a heat burns the outside while the centre stays raw.
Adding cold milk or overworking the potatoes makes the mash gluey, so warm the milk and mash gently.
output.tip: Rinse your hands under cold water before rolling so the mixture does not stick to them.

equipment: Keskmise suurusega kaanega pott riisi jaoks
Suur sügav pann või kastrul kana hautamiseks
steps: Pane riis kaanega potti ja keeda puljongikuubikuta vees vastavalt pakendi juhisele, umbes 12–15 minutit, siis lase kaane all hautuda.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt, kuni riis keeb.
Lõika kanafilee 2–3 cm tükkideks ja kuumuta pannil õli.
Prae kana kõrgel kuumusel 5–6 minutit, siis lisa sibul ja porgand ning prae veel 5 minutit pehmeks.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit, kuni kana on läbi küpsenud.
Sega hapukoor kastmesse, soojenda 2 minutit ilma keetmata ja maitse üle. Soola lisa ainult vajadusel väga vähe, sest puljongikuubik on juba soolane.
pitfalls: Ära lisa lisasoola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik annab juba piisavalt soola ja väikesele lapsele läheb roog liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda kastet pärast hapukoore lisamist tugevalt: hapukoor lõheneb ja kaste muutub tombuliseks.
Ära prae kana liiga tihedalt pannil: liha hakkab hauduma ega pruunistu.
output.tip: Maitsesta kana värskelt jahvatatud pipra või kuivatatud tilliga, siis ei vaja roog soola ja maitse jääb täidlaseks.

equipment: Keskmise suurusega kaanega pott riisi jaoks
Suur sügav pann kana ja kastme jaoks
steps: Pane veekeetja keema ja pane riis kaanega potti: vala peale vesi ning keeda vähese soolaga 12–15 minutit, kuni riis on pehme.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt või lõika õhukesteks ribadeks.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks ja kuumuta pannil õli keskmisel kuumusel.
Prae kana 5–6 minutit, kuni pind on heleda värvusega, lisa sibul ja porgand ning prae veel 4–5 minutit pehmeks.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit, kuni kana on läbi küps.
Sega hapukoor kastmesse, soojenda 1–2 minutit ilma keetmata, maitse ja lisa soola ainult vajadusel; serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kastmesse soola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik on juba soolane ja lapsele läheb roog liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda kastet pärast hapukoore lisamist tugevalt: hapukoor hakkab kalgenema ja kaste muutub terakaks.
Ära lõika kana liiga suurteks tükkideks: need jäävad seest toorelt ja ajakava venib üle 35 minuti.
output.tip: Kasuta puljongikuubikut poole koguse jagu või vähese soolaga puljongit ning lase igaühel soola ise taldrikul lisada, siis sobib roog ka väikesele lapsele.

equipment: Suur sügav pann kanale ja kastmele
steps: Pane veekeetja tööle ja keeda riisile vesi; puljongikuubik jäta hoopis kastme jaoks.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm tükkideks.
Kuumuta pannil õli, hauta sibulat ja porgandit 4–5 minutit pehmeks ning lisa kana.
Küpseta riis kaane all 12–15 minutit, vajadusel lisa pannile veidi vett.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, lisa pannile koos hapukoorega ja hauta 5 minutit; maitsesta soola asemel pipra ja ürtidega.
pitfalls: Ära pane puljongikuubikut ja lisaks palju soola: kuubik on juba soolane ja road muutub lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda kastet hapukoorega tugeval tulel: hapukoor läheb pealt lõhki ja kaste muutub kokku tõmbunuks.
Ära küpseta kanatükke liiga kaua: filee kuivab ja läheb kõvaks.
output.tip: Soola kasta alles taldrikul, pärast maitsmist: nii saab väikese lapse portsu hoida vähesoolasena ja täiskasvanud lisavad ise.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja loputa need enne keetmist kurnikas läbi.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumas rasvas kõrgel kuumusel igast küljest pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae 3 minutit.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed, odrakruubid ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole sisust, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1,5 tundi.
Kupsta kartulid samal ajal kooritult ja tükeldatult ning lisa potti, kui kapsas on 40 minutit haududa saanud.
Sega aeg-ajalt, lisa vajadusel vett ja hauta, kuni kruubid ja liha on pehmed. Maitsesta lõpus soolaga ja tambi kartulid kergelt segu sisse.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab oma tekstuuri.
Ära jäta pada järelevalveta ilma vett lisamata: kruubid imavad vedeliku ja roog kõrbeb põhja.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas ja liha annavad soola ning roog võib üle soolatuks minna.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist kaane all 10 minutit tõmmata, siis muutuvad maitsed ühtlasemaks.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja loputa need sõelal enne keetmist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ning haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumas rasvas igalt poolt pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole segust, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1 tund.
Prae kartulid kooritult tükeldatult kuni poolpehmeks vahepeal ja lisa need potti, kui kapsas on 30 minutit hautatud, ning hauta veel 30 minutit.
Sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel vett, et põhi ei kõrbeks; maitsesta lõpus soola ja pipraga.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma vett lisamata: odrakruubid imavad vedeliku ja põhi kõrbeb.
Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja kaotavad kuju.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas on juba soolane ja roog läheb liiga soolaseks.
output.tip: Lase mulgikapsastel pärast valmimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis ühtlustuvad maitsed ja kruubid paisuvad ilusti.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja pane hapukapsas kurni, et liigne hapuvedelik nõrguks; kui kapsas on väga hapu, loputa seda kergelt.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Pruunista sealiha potis kuumal rasval kõigepealt kuldseks, lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole sisust; hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 30 minutit.
Lisa loputatud odrakruubid ja hauta veel 30 minutit, sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel kuuma vett.
Prae ja koori vahepeal kartulid ning keeda need soolaga pehmeks, 20–25 minutit; serveeri mulgikapsastega kõrvale.
pitfalls: Ära jäta kruupe leotamata ega kapsast kurnamata: kruubid jäävad kõvaks ja roog läheb liiga hapuks.
Ära hauta liiga kuumal tulel ega jäta segamata: roog kõrbeb põhja ja kruubid kleepuvad kinni.
Ära lisa vedelikku korraga liiga palju: roog muutub supiseks, mitte paksuks hautiseks.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis imavad kruubid maitsed paremini sisse.

steps: Kuumuta ahi 200 °C-ni.
Lõika kartulid viiludeks ja laota ahjuplaadile.
Küpseta kartuleid 200 °C ahjus 20 minutit.
Pane lõhe kartulite peale ning maitsesta soola ja sidrunimahlaga.
Küpseta veel 15 minutit, kuni lõhe on läbi küpsenud.
Puista peale tilli.
pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks: nad ei küpse 20 minutiga pehmeks ja jäävad keskelt toored.
Ära jäta lõhet ahju liiga kauaks: kala kuivab ära ja muutub kõvaks.
Ära laota kartuliviile mitme kihina: alumised hauduvad ega saa krõbedaks.
output.tip: Kui lõhel on nahk, pane see allapoole, siis kaitseb nahk liha kuivamise eest.

steps: Kuumuta ahi 200 °C-ni.
Lõika kartulid viiludeks ja laota ahjuplaadile küpsetuspaberi peale.
Küpseta kartuleid 200 °C ahjus 20 minutit.
Pane lõhefilee kartulite peale ja maitsesta soola ning sidrunimahlaga.
Küpseta veel 15 minutit.
Haki till ja puista valmis kala peale.
pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks: need jäävad 20 minutiga keskelt toored.
Ära jäta kartuleid plaadile kuhjadena: viilud hauduvad ja ei küpse ühtlaselt.
Ära küpseta lõhet kauem kui vaja: kala kuivab ja kaotab mahlasuse.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee enne soolamist paberiga, siis jääb pind ahjus ilusam ja maitse selgem.

steps: Kuumuta ahi 200 °C-ni.
Lõika kartulid viiludeks ja laota küpsetuspaberiga kaetud ahjuplaadile.
Küpseta kartuleid 200 °C ahjus 20 minutit.
Pane lõhe kartulite peale ja maitsesta soola ning sidrunimahlaga.
Küpseta veel 15 minutit.
Haki till ja puista valmis roale.
pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks: 20 minutiga need ei küpse läbi ja jäävad keskelt toored.
Ära küpseta lõhet üle ajapiiri: kala kuivab ja kaotab mahlasuse.
Ära pane tilli ahju kaasa: see kaotab värskuse ja tumeneb.
output.tip: Lõika kartuliviilud ühepaksuseks, siis küpsevad need ühtlaselt.
